This report cannot be published yet -- 7 separate issue(s) found, ALL listed here so they can be fixed in one pass rather than one preview_report attempt per issue:
[1] validation refused: the assertion "Warren wrote: 'After the Supreme Court ruled President Trump's tariffs were illegal, the Administration should have done everything in its power to quickly return that money...'" is an attribution, not a claim. Whether someone said it is never the thing under test. Drop the 'X said:' lead, keep the quoted statement as the assertion, and grade THAT against the warehouse (join its components at county, state or year grain and test them) or against independent figures.
[2] validation refused: 1 claim(s) about a government office are graded 'unsupported' without that office's own page being fetched: "The Department of Justice ... will have until Nov. 13 to file its answer ... and until Dec. 9 respond to the motion for relief.". Find the office's release or record, whether or not the article names it, web_fetch it and list that URL in the claim's `sources`. Grade on the evidence found, whoever published it; when that page will not load and nothing found supports the claim, it is 'unsupported'.
[3] validation refused: the article links 12 source(s) and 10 were never fetched: https://fortune.com/2026/11/06/gen-z-voters-midterms-economy-cost-of-living/ , https://fortune.com/2026/07/17/71-billion-tariff-refunds-iran-war-inflation/ , https://fortune.com/2026/02/13/new-york-fed-economists-confirm-americans-footing-trump-tariff-bill/ , https://fiscaldata.treasury.gov/datasets/monthly-treasury-statement/summary-of-receipts-outlays-and-the-deficit-surplus-of-the-u-s-government , https://fortune.com/company/eaton/ , https://www.courthousenews.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/judge-eaton-court-of-international-trade-ieepa-liquidation-process-ruling.pdf , https://fortune.com/2026/06/01/trump-administration-plan-appeal-illegal-ieepa-tariff-universal-refunds/ , https://assets.bwbx.io/documents/users/iqjWHBFdfxIU/r0zJQd82VyFs/v0 , https://www.supremecourt.gov/opinions/24pdf/24a884_8n59.pdf , https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/08/trump-tariffs-democrats-congress-canada.html . web_fetch each one (a 403, 404 or timeout counts as fetched), check the claims that rest on it against what it actually says, then publish again.
[4] validation refused: the assertion "[the order] would return money ... to the more than 330,000 importers of record, whether or not they filed an individual lawsuit against the administration." is graded 'partially false', but its figure '330,000' appears in a source you fetched: https://www.cit.uscourts.gov/sites/cit/files/26-123.pdf page 5: "…nitial order was issued, it was estimated that unlawfully collected duties amounting to $166 billion had been assessed on 53 million entries, involving roughly 330,000 importers of record. See Decl. Brandon Lord (Mar. 6, 2026) ¶ 12, Atmus Filtration, Inc. v. United States, No. 26-01259, ECF No. 31. It was also estimated that …". Re-check the claim against that source, or say in why_not why that passage does not change the grade.
[5] validation refused: the assertion "The Department of Justice ... will have until Nov. 13 to file its answer ... and until Dec. 9 respond to the motion for relief." is graded 'unsupported' with no warehouse figure and no `measure`. search_catalog for the statistic it rests on, with its place, and put that query in `measure`.
[6] validation refused: 1 claim(s) of an attributed figure are graded 'unsupported' with no page read off the article's own site: "The Department of Justice ... will have until Nov. 13 to file its answer ... and until Dec. 9 respond to the motion for relief.". Search for other reporting or the primary record, web_fetch a page that loads and list it in `sources`, then grade on what it says. A Google Drive or Docs viewer page does not count. Grade each figure as its own claim. If no page loads, cite the off-site pages tried and say why in `why_no_page`.
[7] validation refused: claim 2 is grouped `fidelity` and marked `central`: the source audit is not scored, so a central claim there counts for nothing. Remove `central` from it. When the piece repeats the figure as its own assertion, that is a separate `author_claims` claim, and it carries `central` ALSO: claim 6 is graded 'mostly true' with no `inaccuracy`: it MUST state what in the claim differs from the evidence. If nothing in the claim differs from the evidence, the verdict MUST be 'true'; if no evidence was found, it MUST be 'unsupported' ALSO: the author's claims have 0 claims marked `central`: mark exactly one with `central`: true — the assertion that party's case depends on, the one a reader would repeat.

Claims graded purely from publications need no chart.
[3] validation refused: claim 4 is graded 'partially false' and its `inaccuracy` ("The certified class excludes any entity that separately sued; the order reaches non-suing importers (tens of thousands), not all 330,000. An estimate, projection, preliminary, revised or secondary-source figure, or one the warehouse does not hold, MUST NOT be graded below 'true' on that ground. If nothing in the claim differs from the evidence, the verdict MUST be 'true'; if no evidence was found, it MUST be 'unsupported' ALSO: claim 11 fell short of true and supported but carries no valid `errs` (toward_thesis | against_thesis | neutral) ALSO: the claims by Sen.
